content.name: ft_printf.text
content.content:
ft_printf is one of the first 42 projects. Consisting of a function that
mimics the behavior of the 'printf' function from the C standard library.
This project focuses on solidifying the basics of C programming and
prepares the students for the projects that follow in the 42 curriculum.

content.name: get_next_line.text
content.content:
get_next_line (or GNL for short) is a project set on the same level of
complexity as ft_printf, however, instead of focusing on formatting output,
this project focuses on teaching the basics of file I/O operations.
GNL consists of a function that outputs the line after the last one read
from a file.

content.name: push_swap.text
content.content:
push_swap is a step up from all the previous projects, combining all of the
basics and logic learnt. This project aims to introduce the concept of time
and space complexity and program optimization. push_swap requires the student
to make a sorting algorithm under strict rules that performs well with small
and big datasets.

content.name: A-Maze-ing.text
content.content:
A-Maze-ing marks a change in the direction that 42 is heading. Being the first
python project, A-Maze-ing introduces the concept of OOP (Object Oriented Programming)
and programming as a team. The student now has to not only consolidate a new programming
language full of different concepts but also learn how to engineer a maze generator
and solving algorithm, all while learning project and version management for groups.
This is a change in pace and one more critical project to succeed as a 42 student and
software engineer.

content.content:

content.name: About_Me.text
content.content:
Hey, my name is Miguel and I'm a 42 Student and aspiring software developer.
My goal in life ever since I was a kid has been to do something related to science,
and computer science happened to be the field that fascinated me the most, not only for
being open to anyone who has a computer, but also for the complex simplicity behind
everything a computer does. I have always liked to make thoughts real and programming is
the way I found to express my urge to create.
